existing_chapter_text_changes.before: Ask whether the aim is to reduce recurrence risk, control cancer, relieve symptoms or support a local treatment. Your preferences and priorities matter.
existing_chapter_text_changes.after: Discuss how treatment may control the cancer or relieve symptoms, and whether the multidisciplinary team has a separate local-treatment goal. Your preferences and priorities matter. This regimen is for metastatic disease; it is not a routine postoperative recurrence-prevention course.

existing_chapter_text_changes.before: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.
existing_chapter_text_changes.after: For sudden chest pain, collapse or serious breathing difficulty, call 112/999 or seek emergency care immediately. Contact oncology urgently for severe diarrhoea, inability to drink or sudden illness. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

existing_chapter_text_changes.before: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1: oxaliplatin and folinic acid, then fluorouracil bolus and a 22-hour infusion. Day 2: further fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; completion around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.
existing_chapter_text_changes.after: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1: oxaliplatin and folinic acid, then fluorouracil bolus and a 22-hour infusion. Day 2: further fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; completion around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan. Your team confirms the complete Day 2 prescription before treatment.
